reply.summary: Wrote docs/designs/010-lightweight-plan-flow/01-research.md for ADR-010 (selectable `light` plan flow), following the research skill's artifact shape and the lens-suffixed heading style of the 003/006 research docs. Applied three lenses: Prior art, Performance baselines, Platform notes. Findings pin what the design must touch in current code with file/line citations — `decideNext` starts every run at `research` with no `source.kind` branch (states.ts:86-99); `DEFAULT_CONFIG` is the sole budget authority, spread at cli.ts:212/225 and re-defaulted at runner.ts:2068/2126/1940-1943; `runReviewPass` takes `seats: readonly string[]` (runner.ts:1900-1943) and `planPass` is pure over the seat ledger (panel.ts:100-133), so a 2-seat panel is data; the seat stamp is the `02-proposal.md` blob id (runner.ts:199-204, 2416); the size meter is gated by `DESIGN_DOC_STAGES` and today's policy is deliberately warn-not-gate (runner.ts:161-188/1655-1656, report.ts:196-216); `stagePathAllowed` has no flow param and reserves runner names first (gates.ts:283-316); `StateSchema` is `version: 1` with additive-optional-field grammar (state-store.ts:37-64); no `flow` key exists in any checkpoint, prompts, stage registry, skill, or source file. Re-measured all runs from the on-disk checkpoints (sessions = `results` entries, wall clock = sum of `durationMs`): 003 43/2.21 h, 004 53/3.01 h, 005 96/7.05 h, 006 43/3.88 h, 007 44/3.27 h, 008 73/5.78 h — 352 sessions / 25.19 h, 68% in review seats (104 design-review, 89 code-review, 46 editorial-review), 56% in the design phase, and run 004's fix/test-update loop at 14 of 53 sessions; flagged that the ADR's '27 design-review seats for run 005' undercounts the recorded 37, and that LIGHT_CONFIG's maxReviews.code: 6 binds before maxPassesPerRound: 3 × 2 rounds × 2 seats. Prior art cited from primary sources: Rust Forge's heavy/medium/light proposal weights (forge.rust-lang.org/compiler/proposals-and-stabilization.html), Kubernetes KEP-1194 PRR with `kep.yaml` stage metadata and per-stage approvals, PEP 1 ('most enhancements and bug fixes don't need a PEP', `pep-NNNN.rst` next-number allocation), Google eng-practices Small CLs, SWE-book ch. 9 (one reviewer, ~200 lines, diminishing returns of extra reviewers), SmartBear/Cisco (lightweight review <20% of formal time, 20-33% spot checking), Google design docs' 1-3 page mini design doc, aider architect/editor cost results, Anthropic's 15x multi-agent token multiplier, Jekyll custom frontmatter, GitHub Actions paths filters and branch-protection approval counts. Risks and ten designer questions cover the two-seat safety net, the widening ownership spine, budget drift on resume, document/checkpoint flow disagreement on `--force` promotion, the shared NNN space, the cap-reverses-a-documented-lesson tension, and light-on-ADR gate semantics.
reply.commitMessage: docs: research the lightweight plan flow (ADR-010)
docs: design a lightweight plan flow for small work

findings.location: Budget resolution — "maxParallelReviews: // operator knob applied LAST"; Test strategy #14 — "`--extend-budget` on the resume buys sessions under the light cap (the knob an operator actually buys, A16)"
findings.problem: The canonical rule orders `...base` then `...FLOWS[flow].config` and names exactly one knob applied after the flow partial (maxParallelReviews). Any budget raise arriving on the channel the CLI uses (A4's "CLI spread" / `opts.cfg ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG` seams) is therefore overwritten by the flow partial on a light run, so `--extend-budget`, which buys code-review sessions by raising maxReviews.code above the light 6, is silently discarded — Test #14's assertion has no mechanism as the rule is written, and the budget table gives maxReviews no operator path at all. This re-creates the design's own named hidden failure ("Budget drift on resume": operator extends, run escalates again at 6). Introduced by the r1 closure of OQ1/OQ2 (single-resolver rule).
findings.fix: State where a resume-time extension lands: apply it to the output of `configFor` in the same posture as the `maxParallelReviews` line (e.g. `maxReviews: bump(resolved.maxReviews, extend)`), naming that this displaces `...FLOWS[flow].config` as the last writer of maxReviews on a light resume, and assert the extended number in Test #14.

findings.location: Budget resolution, "Which knob binds" — "the reachable shape is exactly `c0` + two dissent passes = 3 two-seat passes" and "`maxPassesPerRound: 3` is the per-round backstop that can only bind at the same point"
findings.problem: The same paragraph says dissent passes are "≤2 seats each", and the funnel keeps "revision to the dissenters only, ratification for stale approvals", so a one-dissenter round runs single-seat passes: c0 (2 sessions) + dissent (1) + ratification (1) = 3 passes at 4 sessions, where maxPassesPerRound: 3 binds first at 4 sessions and the terminal record is `fix-round backstop`, not the 6-session cap. Test strategy #13 is exactly that shape; #14's "escalates at 6 code review sessions" only holds if both seats dissent every pass. So "maxReviews.code: 6 is the binding stop" is shape-dependent, not general.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim: maxReviews.code: 6 binds in the both-seats-dissent shape; maxPassesPerRound: 3 binds first at 4 sessions when a pass runs one seat — and state which escalation string the operator reads in each shape.

findings.location: The `plan` stage (oversized-plan gate) — "a missing section counts as 0 items (a faithfulness concern for the seats, not a gate)"; Risks row 2 — "`planMaxFiles` catches files-spanned"
findings.problem: The file-count gate keys on the bullet count of `## Files to touch`, so a plan that names its files in prose, or under a renamed/absent heading, counts 0 and passes the gate that exists for the very class this design fears (small in lines, wide in consequences). Risks row 2's mitigation claim is therefore formatting-dependent.
findings.fix: Make the section required: deny with `the light plan requires a ## Files to touch section (N files, cap 10)`, replacing the "missing counts as 0" rule and keeping the bullet-count parse.

findings.location: Context — "the same 13-stage, five-seat path"; Compatibility matrix — "13-stage path, 5 seats, budgets unchanged"; Chosen design — "`full` declares today's twelve stages"
findings.problem: The full flow's stage count is stated two ways in one document (13 vs twelve). Test strategy #1 pins `FLOWS.full.stages` to "today's stages exactly", so the count is part of the contract, not prose, and an implementer cannot tell which is the regression baseline.
findings.fix: Use the STAGE_BASES row count in all three places.

findings.location: Budget resolution — "`funnelSpecialties(phase, cfg)` and `states.ts`'s `specialtiesFor(phase, cfg)` read `cfg.reviewSeats` and fall back to the five specialties when absent"; Options — "resolved from the flow exactly once"
findings.problem: The seat fallback exists in two implementations (panel and states), so DEFAULT_CONFIG is not the sole default authority for the seat panel, and the fallback direction is the unsafe one: any light call site handed a config literal that is not configFor output fans out to five seats and looks healthy — the failure mode ADR-010 warns about. The "resolved once" claim does not hold as written.
findings.fix: Export one resolver from flows.ts (e.g. `seatsFor(phase, cfg)`) used by both funnelSpecialties and specialtiesFor, so there is a single fallback and a single place to test; name the residual "absent → full panel" direction in Risks row 4.

findings.location: Test strategy #6 — "`flow: Light` and `flow: sideways` reach a denial"; Selecting the flow — "throws `invalid flow "<value>" for <source>: expected full or light`" and "Unreadable files keep their existing `sourceAdmissible` denial"
findings.problem: #6 and #17 describe the same input with two different outcomes: a source-gate denial in #6, a pre-lock usage error in the prose and in #17. The prose reserves denial for unreadable files. As written, the test contract is ambiguous about which outcome is asserted.
findings.fix: Change #6's verb to the pre-lock usage error and reserve "denial" for the unreadable-file case.

findings.location: The `plan` stage — "It states no number: `{{planMaxLines}}`/`{{planMaxFiles}}` are interpolated into the prompt from the registry"; Options, second entry — "The skill carries the template's five sections and no number"
findings.problem: ADR-010 §Light stages states "The `plan-note` skill carries the template and its length cap". The design's placement (registry owns the numbers, skill carries the template) is argued and sound, but nowhere records that it supersedes the ADR sentence, so the cap's home is stated in two places across the two documents.
findings.fix: Add one clause in The `plan` stage (or Deferred): ADR-010's "skill carries the length cap" is superseded — the skill carries the template, the registry owns the numbers.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Windows | unknown | No Windows CI job exists in this repo; nothing in this design exercises a platform-specific path, and no test claims Windows (Test strategy #21)"
findings.problem: new — the compatibility checklist treats a matrix row reading `unknown` as a major: the design leaves Windows support undefined rather than claimed or refused, so an operator running a light job on Windows gets no support statement to act on, and the row's justification describes the delta ("nothing in this design exercises a platform-specific path") instead of the support surface. The Deferred bullet "A Windows CI job to replace the `unknown` compatibility row — no follow-up yet" is consistent with ADR-010, which never mentions Windows, so the deferral is not re-opened; the row needs a status.
findings.fix: Give the row a definite status in the shape of the row above it: `| Windows | no | The repo's tested support surface is linux; this design adds no Windows-specific path and claims no Windows support (A20, Test strategy #21) |`, and align Test strategy #21's closing clause with it. Add the CI job only if the row is to become `yes`.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Node ≥ 22.23.4 (package `engines`), linux | yes | No new platform surface"
findings.problem: new — the matrix's OS rows are linux and Windows only, so the checklist's platform set (which names macOS) is unaddressed: a reader cannot tell whether a light run is supported on macOS, and the design states its support surface only inside the linux row.
findings.fix: Add one OS-status row that closes the question, e.g. `| macOS | no | Same support surface as Windows: no platform-specific path, no test claims it (A20) |`, and have Test strategy #21 name the OSes the suite actually runs on; claim macOS `yes` only with a #21 entry that runs the suite there, as checklist item 7 requires.

findings.location: Ownership — the security spine, widened in one flow — "`stagePathAllowed(stage, path, flow = 'full')` (A8): `namesReservedSegment(path)` **stays first and wins in both flows**"
findings.problem: new — the design widens `implement`/`fix` write access to test paths through a predicate A8 describes in regex terms (`TEST_PATH_RE`, `namesReservedSegment`), and never states the path form the predicate receives, so both the widening and the reserved-name precedence are decided by string matching on separators and case. Checklist item 6 wants separators and case handled by a library: `tests\x.test.ts` (Windows) or `Tests/x.test.ts` (case-insensitive filesystem) is exactly the string pair that flips a deny into an allow.
findings.fix: Add one clause naming the existing contract as the authority — paths reach `stagePathAllowed`/`ownershipIssue` repo-root-relative and POSIX-normalized by the existing helper, so the added `flow` parameter introduces no new path parsing — and extend Test strategy #7's reserved-name list with a backslash/case-variant path so the precedence is asserted against the normalized form, not only the canonical spelling.

results.failure: independence violation: read a review report: /home/mike/repos/bindforge/docs/designs/010-lightweight-plan-flow/reviews/design/security-r1c0.md

findings.location: Options considered, "Seats in `PipelineConfig`" + Chosen design → Budget resolution: "`funnelSpecialties(phase, cfg)` and `states.ts`'s `specialtiesFor(phase, cfg)` read `cfg.reviewSeats` and fall back to the five specialties when absent"
findings.problem: The review panel — the pipeline's audit gate — becomes unvalidated config data. `configFor` spreads `base` (A4's `opts.cfg`/CLI seam) before `FLOWS[flow].config`, and `FLOWS.full.config` is documented as "an empty partial", so for a full run a caller-supplied `reviewSeats` is the effective panel with no validation anywhere in the design: `reviewSeats.code: []` makes `seatsConverged` vacuously true (A2 lists it as a consumer of the seat list), so `case 'code-review'` converged routes to `doc-sync`/`done` with zero review sessions and no escalation, and `reviewSeats.code: ['corectness']` reaches seat launch with a name no agent backs. The design itself canonicalises the empty list (`reviewSeats.design: []`), so "empty = this phase has nobody" is now legal in the same field that carries the code panel. `planMaxLines`/`planMaxFiles` are equally unbounded. Fix: put the validation in the documented `configFor` contract and replace the bare "fall back to the five specialties when absent" clause (also the truthiness trap for `[]`) with a presence-based read plus rules: every seat name must be one of the five known specialties; the seat list for every phase the flow runs must be non-empty (`design: []` legal only because the registry's `stages` declares no design phase for `light`, not as a tunable); `planMaxLines`/`planMaxFiles` positive integers; violations throw at the same pre-lock posture as the bad `flow` value. Add Test strategy entries: `configFor` rejects an empty code panel for a flow that runs code review, rejects an unknown specialty name, and keeps the registry's two seats when `base.reviewSeats` is supplied for `flow: light`.
findings.fix: State the seat/config validation inside the `configFor` contract (known-specialty names; non-empty panel for every phase the flow runs; positive-integer plan caps; throw pre-lock), replacing the "fall back to the five specialties when absent" clause with a presence-based read plus those rules, and pin it with three Test strategy cases (empty code panel, unknown specialty, base seats overridden by the light registry).

findings.location: The `plan` stage: "`mode: primary`, edits `docs/designs/**`, denies `.pipeline.json`"
findings.problem: The plan's write surface is specified only as agent permissions, and the design's own reasoning says that is not the gate: "the gate is code — agent permissions and skill text are advisory (A13)". The Ownership section's deltas name `implement`/`fix`, "test-engineer stages and document stages", and `stagePathAllowed` keys on the stage name (A8), so the new name `plan` appears in no stated code rule. Test strategy #18 pins only `plan` writing `src/**`, and Test strategy #7's reserved-name enumeration ("`implement`, `fix`, `test-authoring`, `test-update` and document stages") omits `plan`, whose designated directory is exactly where `.pipeline.json` sits.
findings.fix: Add one clause to Ownership: `plan` is governed by the document-stage rule in both flows (writes confined to the run's `docs/designs/NNN-<slug>/` document paths, `namesReservedSegment` first), and add `plan` to Test strategy #7's reserved-name list (`.pipeline.json`, the lock, `ESCALATION.md`, a `saveState` tmp) for both flows.

findings.location: The `plan` stage (Oversized-plan gate) + Risks: "a missing section counts as 0 items (a faithfulness concern for the seats, not a gate)"
findings.problem: The file gate fails open in exactly the case it was added for. It is an exact heading string plus a bullet count, so `## Files to Touch`, `## Files to touch:`, an indented list, or a numbered list all count 0 — "80 lines naming 20 files passes a line count with room to spare" also passes the file count silently. The section the gate reads is the only signal that section carries, and the two seats left are `correctness` and `testing`, not design reviewers, so the stated hand-off to seat faithfulness does not cover it; the mitigation row "`planMaxFiles` catches files-spanned" is then untrue as written.
findings.fix: Make the matcher canonical (case-insensitive exact heading after trimming; items = `-`/`*`/numbered entries at any indent under the section) and treat a missing section as a denial with its own escalation string (`plan names no Files to touch section: set flow: full and re-run with --force`), replacing "a missing section counts as 0 items" — `prompts/plan.md` renders the section, so absence is a contract violation, never a legal plan.

findings.location: Selecting the flow: "`state.flow` is set in `runPipeline` immediately after `freshState`, so **the entry save carries it**"
findings.problem: The section describes two reads — the pre-lock validation "reads the source text right after `deriveIdentity`", then the entry save — and never says the stamped value is the value that passed validation. If the save re-parses, an edit to the source document between the two reads changes the effective flow after the pre-lock usage-error gate approved a different one.
findings.fix: State that the value validated pre-lock is carried on the `deriveIdentity` result and is the sole input to `state.flow`: one frontmatter read per entry, no re-parse at save.

findings.location: Budget resolution — "the reachable shape is exactly `c0` + two dissent passes = 3 two-seat passes … so **`maxReviews.code: 6` is the binding stop**; `maxPassesPerRound: 3` is the per-round backstop that can only bind at the same point"
findings.problem: new — The session cost of a pass is not fixed at 2, so the light code phase has no single binding stop. The funnel the design keeps running unmodified prompts only the dissenters on a revision pass and only the stale approvers on a ratification pass (State graph delta: "revision to the dissenters only, ratification for stale approvals"; Test strategy #13 pins exactly that: "the dissent pass prompts only that seat, and the stale approver runs one ratification pass"). In the single-dissenter shape each pass after c0 costs 1 session, so round 1 is c0(2) + dissent(1) + 3rd pass(1) = 4 sessions when maxPassesPerRound: 3 stops it — the pass backstop binds two sessions before maxReviews.code: 6, not "at the same point". Conversely, since the cap is checked at pass entry (A16), a 2-seat pass launched at 5 spent sessions closes the phase at 7, so "the run escalates at 6 code review sessions" (Test strategy #14) holds only in the widest-dissent case. The knob choice survives — every reachable shape sits in the 4–7 session band, far under the 43-session baseline — but the cost model that ADR-010's OQ1 asked to resolve, and the escalation point the tests assert, are written as exact numbers when they are a range.
findings.fix: State the light code-phase cost as a range: sessions ∈ [4, 7] — the pass-entry cap check admits a pass while spent sessions < 6, so a 2-seat pass can close the phase at 7, and a 1-seat dissent/ratify pass makes maxPassesPerRound: 3 the first stop at 4 sessions. Replace "can only bind at the same point" with that condition, and add the single-dissenter path to Test strategy #14 as a second case (escalation named by maxPassesPerRound at 4 sessions) so the suite does not pin only the widest shape. No knob change needed.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "`--max-parallel 1` (default, serial lane) | yes | Two seats = 2 × per-seat wall clock"
findings.problem: new — The design bounds light sessions (Test strategy #12: "total sessions ≤ 2 + seats × 3") but never states the light wall clock, while the baseline it argues from is quoted in both currencies (ADR-010's table: 43 sessions / 2.2 h for run 003). The serial default is the shape most light runs will run in, so the design claims the win in one currency only, and A25 concedes there is no per-stage duration datum ("per-stage durations were never aggregated"), leaving the operator-facing acceptance number unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add one derived wall-clock bound to Goals or Rollout #6: at the serial default, 8 sessions × 12 min = 96 min worst case, against run 003's 2.2 h baseline, so the first light runs must land under ~1.6 h. This replaces A25's unmeasured acceptance with the target Rollout #6's recorded data settles; it adds no mechanism.

findings.location: Selecting the flow — "`runPipeline` reads the source text right after `deriveIdentity`"
findings.problem: new — The run-start path now reads and frontmatter-scans the source document twice: once pre-lock for the flow value, once at the existing post-lock sourceAdmissible gate the design keeps ("the accepted value is recorded on the `sourceAdmissible` gate line").
findings.fix: Parse once at the pre-lock point and pass the parsed result (the flow value plus the fields sourceAdmissible already consumes) into the post-lock gate, so the gate line records the value from the same parse. The design already needs that threading to print the accepted value, so this removes the second read instead of adding a step.

findings.location: The `plan` stage, `testOwnership` bullet + Assumption register A14 — "the last rendered from the flow into `implement.md:4` and `fix.md:4-5` in place of the hard-coded \"Never edit test files\"" (new)
findings.problem: The `fix` stage has a third live template the design never lists, and it carries the same rule plus the escape hatch to the deleted stage. `runner.ts:1200-1208` (`stageTemplate`) returns `fix-tests.md` for any `fix` entered with `state.testsGreen === false`, with no flow branch; `prompts/fix-tests.md:8-10` says "a test file that is unformatted ... do not touch them: set testsNeedUpdate ... and the test engineer's stage fixes the files it owns", and `:14` says "Never edit test files; if a test itself must change, set testsNeedUpdate in your reply". A light `fix` entered from a red testsGreen gate is told it owns nothing in `tests/**` and is routed to a stage light deletes — exactly the prompt-contradicts-the-ownership-matrix defect A14 was raised to close. `tests/pipeline/fix-trigger.test.ts:31,58` shows the template is live; the design's coverage list (A14, Rollout step 2, Test strategy #11) omits it, so the suite stays green over the gap.
findings.fix: Extend the same `{{testOwnership}}` variable to `fix-tests.md` — no new mechanism, the design's own variable in the third template, with its `testsNeedUpdate` sentence rendering the light branch ("no test engineer exists in this flow"). Add `fix-tests.md` to A14's site list, Rollout step 2, and Test strategy #11's render assertions.

findings.location: Budget resolution — "maxParallelReviews: // operator knob applied LAST / base?.maxParallelReviews ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG.maxParallelReviews ?? 1" (new)
findings.problem: This key is dead logic that hard-codes a third copy of a default. The budget table says the knob is "shared; `--max-parallel` applied last", so no `FLOWS[flow].config` partial sets it: `...base` in the spread already lands the operator's value after the flow partial, and `...DEFAULT_CONFIG` already supplies `1` (`stages.ts:83`). The `?? 1` literal is a pinned default that outlives `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — raise the package default to 2 and `configFor` keeps returning 1 — contradicting the comment on the line above it, "remains the sole default authority (A4)".
findings.fix: Drop the key from the spread and add one clause: "no flow partial may set `maxParallelReviews`, which is why spread order alone satisfies the ADR's applied-last rule." Test strategy #2's "the operator's `maxParallelReviews` intact" assertion covers it unchanged.

findings.location: Budget resolution, seats paragraph — "`funnelSpecialties(phase, cfg)` and `states.ts`'s `specialtiesFor(phase, cfg)` read `cfg.reviewSeats` and fall back to the five specialties when absent" (new)
findings.problem: Those two functions are byte-identical today (`panel.ts:31-32`, `states.ts:25-26`, both `phase === 'code' ? CODE_SPECIALTIES : DESIGN_SPECIALTIES`). Threading `cfg` into both creates two implementations of the seat-resolution rule and two copies of the five-seat fallback — the drift the design cites against a cap living in two places ("a cap in the skill *and* the registry is two authorities that drift"), rebuilt in code. Test strategy #15 asserts the effective numbers, not the seat list, so a divergence between the two resolvers goes uncaught.
findings.fix: Name one resolver: `specialtiesFor(phase, cfg)` delegates to `funnelSpecialties(phase, cfg)` (both are already imported by `runner.ts`), so the `reviewSeats` read and the five-seat fallback exist once. Add a clause noting the direct `DESIGN_SPECIALTIES` use at `states.ts:152` is the editorial path, which light never reaches, so it needs no flow read.

findings.location: The `plan` stage, oversized-plan gate — "when the `## Files to touch` section's bullet count exceeds `cfg.planMaxFiles`" (new)
findings.problem: Two costs for one mechanism. (a) ADR-010 fixes "Two deterministic stops" (the 80-line meter, the budget) and accepts as a cost that "nothing in the tool stops an operator from picking `light`"; the file ceiling is a third stop, and A24 concedes the constant has no datum — "no repo datum measures it". (b) The measured quantity is the bullet count the planner types, not the files the change touches, so the class the gate is for — "small-in-lines, wide-in-consequences" — clears it by grouping 20 files under 8 bullets: a knob whose signal is self-reported prose escalates on formatting while missing the risk it cites.
findings.fix: Count the section's path-shaped tokens (the same path strings `moves.ts`'s ownership predicate reads) rather than bullets, and land the ceiling in the data step the design already has — Rollout 6 settles A23-A25 from the first light runs — so the first merged slice ships the ADR's two stops. If it lands now, say in the gate paragraph that bullet count is a proxy and record the proxy's known miss.

findings.location: The `plan` stage, skill bullet — "Skill `.opencode/skills/plan-note/SKILL.md` (new): the template and its sections" alongside "Template `tools/orchestration/prompts/plan.md` (new) renders the five sections" (new)
findings.problem: The five sections then live in two files — the shape the Options section rejects for the cap ("a cap in the skill *and* the registry is two authorities that drift"). The repo already has the single-source pattern: `prompts/proposal.md` is three lines pointing at `.opencode/skills/design-proposal/references/template.md`, which holds the structure.
findings.fix: Give `prompts/plan.md` the same 3-line pointer shape and keep the section list once, in `plan-note/references/template.md`: the skill owns the sections, the registry owns the numbers.

reply.summary: All five majors and every minor/nit from the four review reports are consumed by changing the design, not appending to it: the 10-file plan gate is deleted (deferred, with A24 and the Risks row it guarded), the `maxParallelReviews` copy is deleted from `configFor`, the seat panel gains one validation contract in `configFor` plus one resolver `seatsFor` that both call sites delegate to, `--extend-budget` is stated as the state-side allowance it is (new A27, verified at runner.ts:2357-2371 — the reported spread-order conflict does not exist, so no last-writer rule was added), the light code-phase cost is restated as the range 4–7 sessions with the two escalation records, `fix-tests.md` joins the `{{testOwnership}}` sites (A14, Rollout 2, Test #11), the Windows row becomes `no` with macOS named beside it, Ownership gains the `plan` document-stage rule and the path-normalization clause, and Selecting the flow collapses to one frontmatter parse. Net +52 lines (484→536) because the round adds a validation contract, one assumption row, one test entry and eight Revision-log entries that the reports required; that is offset by deleting the file-count gate, the duplicated config key, the ADR-inherited Options verbosity and the log's transcript-style entries.

findings.location: Ownership — the security spine, widened in one flow — "Paths reach `stagePathAllowed`/`ownershipIssue` repo-root-relative and POSIX-normalized (A8/A9), so the `flow` parameter parses no path: separator and case variants are settled before the predicate sees them."
findings.problem: new — this is the sentence that keeps the light widening of `implement`/`fix` write access from being decidable by string shape (`TEST_PATH_RE`, `namesReservedSegment`), and it cites (A8/A9), which do not record it: A8's row states the signature, the reserved-segment precedence and the `TEST_PATH_RE` denial; A9's row states only that `moves.ts` validates both endpoints through the same predicate. No register row names who normalizes, so checklist item 6's "separators and case handled by a library, not string concatenation" rests on an uncited assertion, and "POSIX-normalized" names an operation that settles separators, not case, leaving the case half of the sentence without a stated mechanism (its only exposure is a case-insensitive filesystem, which the matrix now declares `no`). My r1 finding is otherwise closed: #7 asserts the normalized-form verdict for separator/case variants.
findings.fix: Name the normalizer as the authority: cite the existing `gates.ts`/`moves.ts` helper/call site that produces the repo-root-relative POSIX path, and extend A8's Basis with that line so the register row carries the claim (marked verified as the rows above it). Add the matching half-clause that no case-folding is performed, so the reserved-name deny and `TEST_PATH_RE` are exact-spelling rules on the supported, case-sensitive linux surface — which is what Test strategy #7's "the verdict of its canonical spelling" asserts.

findings.location: Test strategy #21 and Deferred — "no macOS or Windows job exists, so both compatibility rows read `no` and no test claims them" / "A Windows or macOS CI job to move those compatibility rows from `no` to `yes`"
findings.problem: new — the compatibility matrix states these OSes as a single merged row (`| Windows / macOS | no | …`), so "both rows" and "those rows" point at a table shape the document no longer has; an implementer writing #21 looks for a second row that does not exist.
findings.fix: Make the two references singular: "so the Windows/macOS compatibility row reads `no`" and "…to move the Windows/macOS row from `no` to `yes`".

findings.location: Ownership — the security spine, widened in one flow: "Paths reach `stagePathAllowed`/`ownershipIssue` repo-root-relative and POSIX-normalized (A8/A9), so the `flow` parameter parses no path: separator and case variants are settled before the predicate sees them." + Test strategy #7: "a path spelled with a foreign separator or a case variant arrives normalized and repo-root-relative, so it gets the verdict of its canonical spelling"

The sentence makes the reserved-name precedence (A8's first rule, the guard on `.pipeline.json`, the lock, `ESCALATION.md`, the `saveState` tmp) depend on an upstream path normalizer that the assumptions cited for it do not establish: A8's stated content is "`stagePathAllowed` takes no flow; `namesReservedSegment` runs first; `implement`/`fix` are denied `TEST_PATH_RE`", A9's is "move validation checks both endpoints" — neither records normalization. If the normalizer folds case, the predicate scores a different file than the write — `TESTS/scratch.ts` inherits the light `implement` test-path allow (the widening applied to a path that is not in the test tree on a case-sensitive filesystem), and a document stage's legitimate spelling can be denied. If it leaves case alone, #7 asserts behavior no correct implementation has. findings.location: Budget resolution — "both seats dissenting admits a 2-seat pass at 5 spent and closes the phase at 7 — the shape where **`maxReviews.code: 6`** binds, on the session-budget record" (and Test strategy #14(a))
findings.problem: re-raised (residue of my r1 major, which is otherwise closed: the 4–7 range, the one-dissenter stop at 4, and #14's second case all landed). The shape that closes at 7 is mislabeled, and the mislabel is pinned as a test expectation. In the shape named, every pass is 2 seats (`c0` = both seats, dissent passes = both dissenters), so cumulative spend at a pass entry is 2, 4, 6 — never 5. The third pass is admitted at 4 spent and closes the round at 6, and the cap check at the next pass entry (6 ≥ 6) escalates: that shape closes at **6**, with `maxPassesPerRound: 3` co-binding at the same entry. Reaching 7 requires an odd spend at a pass entry, which only a mixed-width round produces — `c0` 2 + 1-seat dissent 1 + 1-seat ratification 1 = 5 (the funnel's "revision to the dissenters only, ratification for stale approvals"), after which the next round's 2-seat `c0` is admitted at 5 and lands the phase at 7. An implementer driving Test #14(a) as written ("both seats dissent every pass … the phase closing at 7") writes a test whose expected total that shape cannot produce.
findings.fix: In the same two sentences, attribute 6 to the all-2-seat shape (cap and pass backstop co-bind at pass 4's entry) and 7 to the mixed dissent+ratification shape (odd spend at pass entry admits a 2-seat pass), and split Test #14(a) into those two expectations so the suite pins the shape that closes at 6 and the shape that closes at 7. No knob change: the 4–7 band and the `maxReviews.code: 6` / `maxPassesPerRound: 3` / `maxRounds: 2` division stand as written.

findings.location: Rollout #6 — "check them against the derived bound — ≤ 8 sessions, ≤ 96 min at the 12-min stage bound in the serial default, against run 003's 43 sessions / 2.2 h (A25 has no per-stage datum)"
findings.problem: new (introduced by the text written to close my r1 wall-clock finding). The adopted number is Test strategy #12's converged-run ceiling (`2 + seats × 3` = 8, a run with no `fix` stage) stated as the light run's bound. (a) It is not the reachable ceiling: the design's own budget arithmetic allows 2 `fix` stages (`maxRounds: 2` bounds the mutating `fix` loop) plus a 7-session code phase, so the escalated shape reaches 2 (plan, implement) + 7 (review) + 2 (`fix`) = 11 sessions, ≤ 132 min at the serial default. A light run that escalates — i.e. behaves as designed — breaks the 8/96 figure, so Rollout 6's recorded data reads as a missed target in the normal case. (b) 12 min per session is the stage *timeout* ceiling, and the same sentence concedes A25 has no per-stage datum; the baseline the row quotes implies ~3.1 min per session (2.2 h / 43), so the light class's expected wall clock is ~12–25 min, not 96. A timeout ceiling applied to the converged session count is an acceptance number that cannot fail, which is the measurement the rollout exists to make.
findings.fix: In the same bullet state the two bounds the design already supports: converged-with-one-`fix` ≤ 8 sessions, escalated ≤ 11 sessions (≤ 132 min ceiling), plus the baseline-implied expectation from run 003's measured mean per-session duration (~3 min → ~12–25 min for a 4–8-session light run), so the recorded sessions and wall clock have a target they can miss. Nothing added: the ceiling stays the registry value it is, and Rollout 6's data step is unchanged.

findings.location: Budget resolution, "Which knob binds in the light code phase" + Test strategy #14(a) — "both seats dissenting admits a 2-seat pass at 5 spent and closes the phase at 7 — the shape where `maxReviews.code: 6` binds, on the session-budget record"
findings.problem: The light flow cannot reach that record, and 7 is not reachable in that shape. reviewSessionsUsed counts per-seat sessions (panel.ts:50-52, results entries `code-review:<specialty>`), and a dissent keeps the same round (states.ts:83: `review('code', open.length > 0 ? state.codeRound : state.codeRound + 1)`), so the both-seats shape is one round of three passes: 2+2+2 = 6 sessions, with pass entries at spent 0, 2, 4 — `spent >= cap` (runner.ts:2357-2359) never fires and spent is always even, so "5 spent" and "closes at 7" are unreachable. The next planPass returns {kind:'blocked'} at `cycle >= cfg.maxPassesPerRound` (panel.ts:113-119), which decideNext escalates (states.ts:183): the terminal record is `code review: pass backstop: 3 review passes already run in this code round (cap 3 passes per round) — the funnel is not converging` at 6 sessions. With 2 seats a round's 3 passes cost exactly the cap, so maxPassesPerRound: 3 prints on every shape (6 sessions both seats dissenting, 4 with one dissenter) and maxReviews.code: 6 never prints. Test #14(a) asserts an escalation record and session count the cited mechanism cannot produce, so implementation chases the test.
findings.fix: Pick one and name the mechanism. (a) Keep maxPassesPerRound: 3 and rewrite the paragraph to: the pass-backstop record prints at 6 sessions (both seats dissenting) and 4 (one dissenter); maxReviews.code: 6 is the ceiling it coincides with, not the string an operator reads — and make #14(a) assert the pass-backstop string at 6 sessions with the light suffix. (b) If the session-budget string is meant to be the light cap's record (ADR-010: "Budget exhaustion … the reason names the flow"), set light maxPassesPerRound: 4, so a pass entry at spent 6 hits `spent >= cap` and prints `code review session budget exhausted (6/6 sessions)`; then state the per-round band as 4–8 sessions and drop "closes at 7" (it needs a 1-seat pass leaving 5 spent).

No register row names the code that canonicalizes paths, rejects absolute forms, or rejects `..`, so the claim the security argument rests on is not confirmable from the design's own inputs, and no behavior is stated for a path that arrives non-canonical — it silently inherits the verdict of a spelling the predicate did not intend (checklist 3, 7). Test strategy #7 compounds it: the clause "a path spelled with a foreign separator or a case variant arrives normalized and repo-root-relative, so it gets the verdict of its canonical spelling" asserts a property of the ingestion plumbing, while #7 is a unit test of the predicate, which cannot observe what it is handed.

findings.location: Budget resolution / Test strategy #14(a) — "both seats dissenting admits a 2-seat pass at 5 spent and closes the phase at 7" and "(a) both seats dissent every pass — escalation on the session-budget record at 6 spent (not 20), the phase closing at 7"
findings.problem: new — the shape named cannot reach 7 under the design's own cap semantics. With the cap checked at pass entry against sessions spent (A16), a pure both-seats-dissent round is a run of 2-seat passes: 2, 4, 6 spent, so the last pass is admitted at 4 spent and the phase closes at 6 — escalation and closure land on the same number. 5 spent only occurs when a 1-seat pass lands in between, i.e. the mixed dissent/ratification shape (c0 2 + 2-seat dissent 2 + 1-seat ratify 1 = 5, then an admitted 2-seat pass closes at 7). As written, #14(a) pins a test to a session count the described shape does not produce, and the cap-binding shape is attributed to the wrong dissent pattern; the 4–7 band and the knob choice survive.
findings.fix: In Budget resolution attach 7 to the mixed shape — "a pass entered below the cap overshoots it: the dissent/ratification alternation reaches 5 spent and closes at 7; the pure both-dissent shape closes at 6 on the session-budget record" — and in #14(a) assert closure at 6, with the 7 overshoot pinned as its own alternating-dissent case so the pass-entry rule stays covered. No knob change, no mechanism added.

findings.location: Rollout 6 — "check them against the derived bound — ≤ 8 sessions, ≤ 96 min at the 12-min stage bound in the serial default, against run 003's 43 sessions / 2.2 h"
findings.problem: new — the stated bound is the converging shape's, not the worst case the same document derives. 8 sessions is Test strategy #12's 2 + seats × 3 (plan + implement + 6 code sessions). The escalated shapes costed out in Budget resolution add the mutating fix rounds: 1 plan + 1 implement + 2 fix (maxRounds: 2) + 6–7 code sessions = 10–11 sessions, i.e. 120–132 min at the 12-min bound — the top of that band is run 003's 2.2 h exactly, so at the serial default a light run that fights is at parity with the baseline the design claims to beat. Stated as the derived bound, the first light runs have no expectation for the escalation path and the headline win is unqualified for it.
findings.fix: Name the shape: "≤ 8 sessions / ≤ 96 min for a run that converges (Test strategy #12's bound); an escalated round reaches 10–11 sessions ≈ 120–132 min at the same bound, at parity with run 003's 2.2 h" — so the recorded data has a target for both shapes. Text only, no mechanism.

findings.location: Rollout 6 + A25 + Risks — "≤ 96 min at the 12-min stage bound" against A25's "A 12-minute stageTimeoutMs is enough for the light flow's plan/implement stages" and the Risks row "12-minute stage timeout is too tight for a light implement"
findings.problem: new — the new wall-clock bound multiplies 12 min by every session, and the majority of the light flow's sessions are code-review seats (6 of the ≤ 8 in #12's shape), while A25 and that Risks row register the timeout's adequacy for plan/implement only. The acceptance target Rollout 6 settles therefore rests on a per-session duration assumption for the flow's dominant session class that no assumption row and no risk carries, and A25 itself concedes per-stage durations were never aggregated.
findings.fix: Widen A25's wording and the Risks row to name the code-review seats as the sessions the 12-min bound covers, and have Rollout 6 record per-session durations for review passes beside the run totals. Registry wording plus one recorded column; no mechanism.

findings.location: Budget resolution, seats paragraph — "`funnelSpecialties` (`panel.ts:31-32`) and `states.ts`'s byte-identical `specialtiesFor` (`states.ts:25-26`) delegate to it, so the `reviewSeats` read and the five-seat fallback live once, in one test" (new)
findings.problem: The delegation has no route for `cfg`, and the route it needs is the signature fan-out the Options section says the design avoided. `funnelSpecialties(phase)` is called from `dissentingSeats`, `staleSeats`, `seatsConverged`, `planPass` and `seatSummary` (`panel.ts:57,68,77,103-104,184`), and only `planPass` takes `cfg`; `specialtiesFor(phase)` is called from `runner.ts:2322,2332,2339,2345,2617`, none with `cfg`. findings.fix: Add one clause naming the four signatures that gain `cfg` (`dissentingSeats`, `staleSeats`, `seatsConverged`, `seatSummary`) and stating that the effective config is already in scope at each of their call sites — `planPass`, `decideNext`, the status lines, `escalationMarkdown` — so nothing outside the funnel learns the seat list; and reword Options' rejection to what it rejects, a seat-list parameter threaded into the funnel from outside. findings.location: Budget resolution + Test strategy #14(a) — "The session cap is checked at **pass entry**, ahead of that backstop (A16), so it never fires: `maxReviews.code: 6` is the ceiling the backstop coincides with, not a string an operator reads" / "#14(a) … the session-budget string never printing (Budget resolution)"
findings.problem: regression introduced by the closure of r1 #1: the replacement text asserts a universal negative that holds only for the single-round shape. Session accounting is phase-side and cumulative across rounds (full's `design: 40` exceeds one round's 5 seats × 6 passes = 30, so the cap spans rounds), and `maxRounds: 2` lets the code phase span two code-review rounds: R1 `c0` 2 sessions + one dissent pass 1 = 3 spent, dissent routes to `fix`, R2 `c0` enters at 3 and closes at 5, a pass entered at spent 5 is admitted and closes at 7, and the next pass entry at 7 is refused by the cap — the session-budget record prints. So the cap is the binding stop on the multi-round shape and the real phase ceiling is 7 sessions, not 6. The knob values and the cost bound r1 approved are unaffected; the terminated-shape attribution that Rollout 6's escalated band and #14 read from this paragraph is now wrong.
findings.fix: Scope the sentence: "the pass backstop terminates a single-round phase at 4 or 6 sessions; a phase that spans both `fix` rounds accumulates past the cap, so the session-budget record is the terminal string there and the phase ceiling is 7." Keep #14(a) as shape (a) (correct there) and name the multi-round cap-firing case as the shape that prints the session-budget record. Text plus one integration case; no knob, no mechanism.

findings.location: Rollout 6 — "a run that escalates legitimately sits above it, at **10–12 sessions** (Budget resolution)"
findings.problem: The escalated band's top is one session above what the section it cites allows, and the band is newly written text from the r1 #2 closure, so the recorded-data target for the escalation path is off. Under the design's own arithmetic the fighting run is 1 `plan` + 1 `implement` + 2 `fix` (maxRounds 2) + the code-phase ceiling of 7 (a pass entered at spent 5, closing at 7) = 11 sessions; 12 is unreachable because a pass entered at 6 or more is refused. The number's purpose is the wall-clock reading: 11 × 12 min = 132 min = run 003's 2.2 h, the parity point the document concedes; 12 sessions reads as 144 min, i.e. the light flow losing to the baseline it exists to beat, which the cited section does not support.
findings.fix: "a run that escalates legitimately sits above it, at 10–11 sessions ≈ 120–132 min at the same 12-min bound — parity with run 003's 2.2 h (Budget resolution)." Text only.

findings.location: State graph delta, escalation-suffix paragraph — "The light suffix is appended to every code-phase escalation the light flow reaches: `decideNext`'s pass-backstop string (`states.ts:183`) and fix-round string (`states.ts:187-194`), and the runner's round-entry `code review revise-round backstop reached (2/2 rounds)`" (new)

The session cap is per-phase cumulative (`reviewSessionsUsed` counts every `code-review:` result in the run, `runner.ts:2358` + `panel.ts:50-52`) while `maxPassesPerRound` is per-round, so `maxReviews.code: 6` equals one non-converging round's ceiling and is spent inside round 1; any later code-round entry satisfies `spent >= cap` and escalates on the session-budget string at `runner.ts:2362-2368`, a code-phase escalation the light flow reaches that the list omits. findings.location: Rollout 6 — "a run that escalates legitimately sits above it, at 10–12 sessions (Budget resolution)" (new)

With `maxReviews.code: 6` as a phase-cumulative cap, a light run's code phase cannot reach 12 sessions: plan 1 + implement 1 + fix rounds + at most 6 code sessions, so the escalated ceiling is about 9 sessions plus the `--extend-budget` grants the operator buys. findings.location: State graph delta — "gated on `flowOf(state) === 'light'` and `state.lastStage` in `implement`/`fix`/`code-review`: one append covers every escalation those stages reach"
findings.problem: new. The gate is a hand-written triple of three of the light flow's four stages, and this revision deleted the clause that justified the exclusion ("skips the plan stop, whose string already names the flow and the promotion recipe"). The triple excludes more than the plan-size stop: every escalation a light `plan` reaches lands in `finalizeEscalate` with `lastStage: 'plan'` — the 12-minute `stageTimeoutMs` (`runner.ts:1343`), the stage-failure escalations (`runner.ts:2249,2283`), the gate escalations (`runner.ts:2569`) — so a light run that stalls in `plan` prints no flow, against ADR-010's Status clause ("An escalated light run must read as 'this was too big for the light flow', not as an unexplained stall") and this design's own Risks mitigation "the escalation names the flow, so an operator reads it as a light-flow limit", which the stage set satisfies for `implement` only. It is also the flow's stage list written a second time, so a registry gain of a stage silently stops naming the flow — against the registry-as-data goal in ADR-010's Consequences.
findings.fix: Key the append on the flow's declared stages (`FLOWS[flow].stages`, registry data) and exclude the plan-size stop by the string the gate composes (that text already names the flow and `--force`); state in The `plan` stage that a light `plan` timeout or stage failure carries the suffix. Same single append site, one enumeration removed rather than added.

findings.location: Flow registry — "The one seat-panel resolver; `funnelSpecialties` and `specialtiesFor` delegate to it. `export function seatsFor(phase: ReviewPhase, cfg: PipelineConfig)`"
findings.problem: new. The resolver is typed over three phases while the config it reads governs two: `reviewSeats` has `design` and `code` keys, and `ReviewPhase` also carries `editorial`, which `specialtiesFor` is called with (`runner.ts:2322-2345`). The "one place" resolver therefore needs a third branch answering from the five-seat constant, and the document never says which value it returns for a light run.
findings.fix: Type the resolver with the panel's own `FunnelPhase` (`'design' | 'code'`) — exactly the phases `reviewSeats` has keys for — and leave the editorial answer in `specialtiesFor`, where the design already places it (`states.ts:152` keeps `DESIGN_SPECIALTIES`, editorial only). One type narrowed; no new code.

findings.location: Budget resolution, "Which knob binds in the light code phase" — "The session cap is checked at **pass entry**, ahead of that backstop (A16), so inside the first code round the backstop prints first."
findings.problem: re-raised (partially closed). The false prediction "so it never fires" is gone, and the new cumulative-cap sentence is sound: reviewSessionsUsed counts every `code-review:` result (panel.ts:50-51), so the cap binds only at a pass entry in a later code round, which the `--stage code-review` force example reaches and #14(c) asserts. The causal clause is unchanged from r1c1 finding 2: read literally, "cap checked at pass entry, ahead of the backstop" predicts the session-budget string at spent 6, which #14(a) says never prints in that round. The reason the backstop wins inside the first round is upstream — decideNext calls planPass (states.ts:181) and escalates the blocked pass-backstop reason (states.ts:183) at the top of the drive-loop iteration, before the review branch reaches runner.ts:2357 — so the iteration at spent 6 ends in escalation and no pass entry happens at the cap.
findings.fix: Replace the `so`-clause's basis: "the pass backstop is decided upstream, in decideNext's planPass call (states.ts:181-183), so the iteration at spent 6 escalates on it and no pass entry happens at the cap."

findings.location: Rollout 6 — "a run that escalates legitimately sits above it, at ≈ 9 sessions — plan 1, implement 1, the fix rounds, and at most the code phase's 6 cumulative (Budget resolution)"
findings.problem: new. The named components sum to 10, and they cannot all be maximal at once: 6 cumulative code sessions is the pass-backstop shape, which dies inside the first round and spends no fix session (1+1+6 = 8), while the 2 fix rounds is the round-entry shape, which reaches only 4 code sessions (1+1+2+4 = 8). findings.problem: new text from the r1 #2 closure; the band's value is not the sum of the components the same sentence lists. And the shape that escalates without a force — the round-entry backstop at 2/2 after two fix sessions, the code phase closing at its in-round 4 (this section's one-dissenter pass-backstop figure) — is 1+1+2+4 = 8, which is exactly #12's converging bound (`2 + seats × 3` = ≤ 8), so it does not "sit above it". The escalated band is the recorded target for the escalation path, the datum Rollout 6 collects and A23/A25 settle against; as written it states one value no shape produces (9), hides the decomposition's ceiling (10), and asserts a separation from the converging bound that the 8-session shape contradicts. The direction survives at both ends — 8–10 sessions at the 12-min bound is 96–120 min against run 003's 43 sessions / 2.2 h — so only the band's arithmetic is wrong. No knob, no mechanism. (r1 #1 is closed correctly: the cap claim is now scoped, phase-cumulative accounting is cited, and #14(c) asserts the session-budget record; r1 #2's 12 is gone, its replacement is the defect.)

findings.location: Chosen design — The `plan` stage, `plan` agent bullet — "denies `.pipeline.json`, reads and writes `transcripts/**`, and allows shell."

findings.location: The `plan` stage, first bullet (planner agent) — "`mode: primary`, edits `docs/designs/**`, denies `.pipeline.json`, reads and writes `transcripts/**`, and allows shell."
findings.problem: The editorial diff rewrote this line ("denies `.pipeline.json`, reading/writing `transcripts/**`, and shell" → "denies `.pipeline.json`, reads and writes `transcripts/**`, and allows shell"), turning two denials into grants, so the changed text creates a security defect that my r1 pass had no basis to raise. The bullet claims the agent is "the `design/designer` shape (A12), one line narrower", and that shape is the opposite on both axes: designer.md:14-22 denies edit AND read of `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**` and denies `shell: "*"`, and researcher.md:14-22 is identical — no document-stage primary agent holds either privilege. (a) Least privilege / audit integrity (checklist item 6): transcripts are the run's record, written by the runner (prompts.ts:79, runner.ts:1640), and runner.ts:1436-1441 states "Transcripts are out of band for every stage", with independence.ts:6-16 failing the attempt outright on a completed transcripts access; an agent granted write over `transcripts/**` can forge the run record that the ownership matrix and the independence audit exist to protect, and granting it read is the run-003 behaviour that produced the fence. (b) The stated privilege set is not implementable: a planner built to this line fails its own stage audit on the first transcripts access. The `allows shell` widening has no stated need — a plan stage runs no commands, designer.md:20-22 denies shell outright, coder.md:26-46 denies `shell "*"` then names seven specific commands, and independence.ts:39-48 records that an obfuscated shell command is the one access the audit provably cannot catch, so an unrestricted shell grant on a primary agent is exactly the privilege the defence-in-depth does not cover. The edit also makes "one line narrower" false, since the sentence adds grants rather than removing lines. The rest of the diff is language-only: the "same pre-lock posture as a bad `flow` value" hunk sharpens the fail-closed claim (consistent with ADR-010's "before the lock and before any inference"), the seat-reader, `the last`→`the latter`, `heavy/heavier flow`→`full flow`, and Rollout reflow hunks touch no security property, and no new dependency is named, so the advisory check has nothing to evaluate.
findings.fix: Restore the pre-diff privileges in that bullet: "denies `.pipeline.json`, reading/writing `transcripts/**`, and shell" — i.e. `shell: "*"` deny and `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**` read+edit deny, mirroring designer.md:11-22. If a light `plan` genuinely needs to run a command, replace the `allows shell` clause with the explicit allowlist shape coder.md:29-46 uses and state the need in the same line; do not add a grant alongside it.

findings.location: The `plan` stage — agent bullet: "`mode: primary`, edits `docs/designs/**`, denies `.pipeline.json`, reads and writes `transcripts/**`, and allows shell."
findings.problem: regression introduced by this editorial hunk. Pre-diff the text read "denies `.pipeline.json`, reading/writing `transcripts/**`, and shell", i.e. all three denied, which is exactly the cited `design/designer` shape (`designer.md:11-22` denies `.pipeline.json`, denies `edit` and `read` on `docs/designs/**/transcripts/**`, denies `shell: "*"`). The rewrite scopes the list the other way and turns the denials into grants, changing technical meaning in a language-only pass. Consequences: (a) the sentence is no longer "the `design/designer` shape … one line narrower" — it cites a record that denies all three; (b) the grants have no consumer in the design, and transcripts are runner-written, not stage input, with the harness failing an attempt on any transcripts access (`coder.md:51-54`, `test-engineer.md:50-52`), so an agent built as written collides with the shared harness the Goals bullet promises to keep "unchanged"; (c) `shell` with no resource scope widens a document-stage agent's surface beyond every existing document agent (designer and researcher deny `shell: "*"`; coder denies it and adds only narrow command allows), and this widening is not recorded in the Risks table the Ownership row relies on. Complexity checklist 1 and 6: unneeded surface, capability with no consumer.
findings.fix: Restore the denials and drop the width claim: "`mode: primary`, edits `docs/designs/**`, denies `.pipeline.json`, denies `transcripts/**` for read and edit, and denies shell — `design/designer`'s rule set verbatim (`designer.md:4-22`)". If shell is genuinely required, name a scoped command allow as coder does (e.g. `npm run check*`) instead of `shell: "*"`, and add the widening to the Ownership Risks row.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/states.ts:224-233 (read with tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:2576-2610 and states.ts:78-80)
findings.problem: The over-cap round guard is ungated, so it truncates the full flow's --extend-budget on the code phase. In the full flow, runner.ts:2577-2601 consumes an extensionRounds grant and charges the round, so codeRound can legitimately become maxRounds + 1; the first decideNext after that round's first pass hits `state.codeRound > cfg.maxRounds`, which fires ahead of the grant-aware budgetLeft and ahead of planPass. The granted round then runs exactly one pass: its dissent never reaches the fix the grant paid for, a pending ratify pass cannot run, remaining grants are dead, and the run escalates with `code review: the fix-round backstop is exhausted (round N)` — a string with no --extend-budget hint, whose footer offers a plain `pipeline resume` that re-escalates on the same line. The design phase has no such round-number guard (states.ts:156/194), which is why budget.test.ts:193-261 stays green while pinning only the design phase. This erodes the ADR/proposal Non-goal "no change to the full … [elided by the checkpoint cap]
findings.fix: Make the guard mean what the grant means, in the flow the design bounds: gate it as `flowOf(state) === 'light' && state.codeRound > cfg.maxRounds`, or make it grant-aware as `state.codeRound > cfg.maxRounds && (state.extensionRounds ?? 0) <= 0`, so the light flow keeps its hard cap while a full-flow granted over-cap round can run its passes and answer its dissent. Then pin it in tests/pipeline/budget.test.ts with a full-flow `resume --stage code-review --extend-budget 1` case asserting the granted round runs more than one pass and spends its grant with an operatorExtension line, beside the light reading at light-budget.test.ts:280-297.

findings.location: tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/runner.ts:2231-2234 and 2294-2303 (consumer: states.ts:78-80)
findings.problem: A light --extend-budget increments state.extensionRounds, which the light flow never consumes. After the round-1 fix the grant is inert (fail-closed, so not the bypass reported in round 1), but it leaves record residue: the checkpoint accumulates a number with no reader, no operatorExtension line ever names it, and statusLines/escalationMarkdown print no grant at all, so an operator reading a light checkpoint sees a standing round-extension count that buys nothing — the same record-honesty shape as the round-1 finding, on the harmless side. Promotion cannot carry it into a live consumer: runPipeline builds freshState, so a --force full entry inherits no light grants.
findings.fix: Charge only the half the flow spends: at both entry sites, increment extensionSessions alone when flowOf(state) === 'light'; or keep the increment and gate-log it once at grant time with the reason that the light flow sets no round cap to extend, so the record states what the grant did not buy. Assert in light-budget.test.ts that extensionRounds is absent (or logged) on a light grant.
